summary: This function extracts text from various document formats by either reading them directly (for plain text files) or converting them first using a tool called docling-convert (for binary formats like PDF and Word documents). It's a shared utility used by other AI tools in this script collection to prepare documents for processing.

explanations.10: The :e:l syntax extracts the file extension and converts it to lowercase — so 'file.PDF' becomes 'pdf'. This makes the case statement work regardless of how the user capitalized the extension.
explanations.17: This checks if the docling-convert command exists and is runnable; if not, the function fails early rather than trying to run a command that doesn't exist.
explanations.22: The :h syntax gets the directory path of the file (everything before the last slash), like turning '/path/to/file.pdf' into '/path/to'.
explanations.23: The :t syntax gets just the filename without the directory path, like turning '/path/to/file.pdf' into 'file.pdf'.
explanations.24: The %.*  pattern removes the last dot and everything after it (the extension), so 'file.pdf' becomes 'file'.
explanations.27: The ( cd "$dir" && ... ) runs the command in a subshell after changing to the file's directory, so docling-convert writes its output files in the right place. The || { ... } catches if the conversion fails.
